title: Lakhpat Rai’s Humiliation and the Opening of Ram Rauni

blocks.text: Kaura Mal’s revenge is public and degrading rather than merely administrative. Lakhpat Rai is chained, disgraced before others, and finally thrown into a sewage pit so that punishment mirrors the moral filth the text attributes to his conduct.

The page uses that humiliation to close one episode cleanly. The poet marks the sequence as completed, ending the account of retribution against a persecutor whose power once seemed unassailable after the massacre.

At once the narrative opens Ram Rauni and shifts back to the Khalsa. Hardship has taught the Singhs that they cannot live forever in scattered wandering, so they begin debating whether a defended position should be raised near Amritsar.
